stem.text: The graph shows the variation with time of the displacement $X$ of a gas molecule as a continuous sound wave passes through a gas.

stem.alt: Graph of displacement X against time in μs, with time axis marks 0 to 1000, showing a continuous wave with two complete cycles.

stem.text: The velocity of sound in the gas is $330\,\text{m s}^{-1}$. All the graphs below have the same zero time as the graph above.
What is the displacement-time graph for a molecule that is a distance of $0.165\,\text{m}$ further away from the source of the sound?

A.alt: Graph of displacement X against time/μs, with time axis marks 0 to 1000, showing a wave that starts at a positive value at time 0.

B.alt: Graph of displacement X against time/μs, with time axis marks 0 to 1000, showing a wave that starts at zero at time 0 and falls first.

C.alt: Graph of displacement X against time/μs, with time axis marks 0 to 1000, showing a wave that starts at a negative value at time 0.

D.alt: Graph of displacement X against time/μs, with time axis marks 0 to 1000, showing a wave that starts at zero at time 0 and rises first.
